messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH p99 streaming latency spike detected for model redwood-xl-3b in us-west-2, affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-3. p99 jumped from 180ms -> 1.8s at 2026-03-15T01:02:34Z. alert id: ALRT-7821
jamie (eng-oncall): seeing it on the dashboard too. p95 up but p99 is crushing streaming tails. is this correlated with the TRT8 kernel rollout?
sophia (eng-runtime): we rolled trt8-kernel v2.3.0 to canary yesterday and started a gradual region rollout ~00:40Z. initial perf looked fine in synthetic tests but not real streaming.
raj (eng-sre): paging triage: are there paging/prefetch errors in dmesg or OOMs?
jamie (eng-oncall): checking node logs now. one node shows repeated kernel WARN and swap churn. infra-bot: attaching last 200 lines of kernel log: ```Mar 15 00:58:41 gpu-node-12 kernel: nvdec: page-in stall 0x3f8`
Mar 15 00:58:42 gpu-node-12 kernel: mm: async page fault handler slowed```
jamie (eng-oncall): also seeing decode stall traces in serve logs, stack shows flash-attn kernel entry.
sophia (eng-runtime): this smells like a compilepath change interacting with FlashAttention/TensorRT kernels — maybe a codegen or alignment regressed. we've got kernel build id: trt8-kernel-v2.3.0-commit: b9f7c4.
lisa (customer-success): FYI customer acme-inc reported timeouts on streaming sessions ~00:59Z, some dropped sessions and client retries. will escalate to them as we triage.
raj (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel on affected nodes, 2) route streaming traffic to older kernel pool or fallback quantized model, 3) scale out to reduce queueing while we debug.
jamie (eng-oncall): can we pin to trt7-compat pool? we still have a small pool running older kernel but it's low capacity.
sophia (eng-runtime): action plan: short-term: switch routing for streaming route /v1/chat/stream to fallback-model redwood-xl-3b-quantized and limit concurrency per-instance to 2, enable prefix cache warmup. medium: roll back trt8-kernel to v2.2.5 in us-west-2 and redeploy after smoke. long-term: revert problematic compiler flag.
jamie (eng-oncall): executing fallback now: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/reroute -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","fallback":"redwood-xl-3b-quantized"}'`
infra-bot: re-route accepted. traffic shift starting, expected convergence ~30s.
jamie (eng-oncall): applying concurrency cap to pool: `rbctl set-concurrency dedicated-gpu-pool-3 2`
aaron (eng-platform): suggest temporarily cordoning nodes with trt8-kernel to prevent new pods landing during rollback.
raj (eng-sre): I'm starting a kernel rollback on the 6 most impacted nodes -> plan: drain, replace kernel, restart worker. ETA ~20-30m.
sophia (eng-runtime): found a suspicious compile flag in v2.3.0: `-DFLASH_ATTENTION_UNSAFE_ALIGN=1` set by default. older builds had it unset. that could change memory alignment assumptions used by flash-attn kernels.
jamie (eng-oncall): could definitely explain tail faults. any quick test to validate?
sophia (eng-runtime): I'll build a debug image with the flag disabled, run a short streaming workload with real request traces against canary pool. command: ```# build
make kernel BUILD_TAG=trt8-v2.3.0-debug CFLAGS='-DFLASH_ATTENTION_UNSAFE_ALIGN=0'
# deploy to canary
kubectl apply -f kernel-canary-deploy.yaml
# run streaming load
wrk -t8 -c100 --script=streaming.lua http://canary-gateway/stream
```
jamie (eng-oncall): good. meanwhile metrics: p99 trending back down to ~420ms after fallback, p95 ~220ms. still above targets but better. customer-impact: acme-inc saw 4% request error rate during spike, total affected sessions ~150 in the window.
lisa (customer-success): pinged acme-inc with mitigation steps and ETA for rollback. they asked for exact rollback time — told them 30-45m.
raj (eng-sre): rollback complete on 4/6 nodes so far. two nodes pending config propagation. will confirm once all show trt8-kernel v2.2.5.
infra-bot: node status update: gpu-node-{12,19,21,24}: kernel v2.2.5, drained -> ready. gpu-node-33, gpu-node-37: rollback in progress.
jamie (eng-oncall): after rollback p99 back to ~190ms on those nodes. global p99 at 260ms. that's within SLO for now.
sophia (eng-runtime): debug canary build queued. if that reproduces locally we'll revert the compile flag in the next kernel patch. also adding a unit test to the build that runs micro-bench with flash-attn loops.
raj (eng-sre): opened incident ticket INC-7821 with RCA placeholder "compile flag changed alignment -> kernel flash-attn memory alignment mismatch -> decode stalls under streaming workload".
jamie (eng-oncall): escalation: loop in runtime leads to patch and CI check. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-platform.
aaron (eng-platform): planning a staged redeploy: disable unsafe align, canary 1%, monitor 15m, then region rollouts. put automatic rollback if p99 rises >30% from baseline.
sophia (eng-runtime): adding the following to rollout policy: ```- rollout: trt8-v2.3.1
  canary: 1%
  duration: 15m
  rollback-if: p99 > 1.3x baseline```
jamie (eng-oncall): customer impact note: acme-inc followup scheduled 02:30Z. cs asked for timeline to ensure no SLAs impacted. recorded incident severity P2 due to partial outage for streaming.
lisa (customer-success): sending summary to acme-inc and affected customers now.
raj (eng-sre): monitoring post-rollback for 1 hour. will keep watch for paging churn or similar spikes.
jamie (eng-oncall): handoff for night shift -> next oncall: @sophia (in case runtime patch needs immediate rollback), @raj for SRE monitoring, @aaron for platform rollout. Handoff checklist: 1) confirm no re-roll of trt8-kernel v2.3.0, 2) watch p99/p95 dashboards, 3) verify canary debug build results and open PR to revert compile flag if reproduces.
sophia (eng-runtime): I'll post build results in this thread when available. started canary run now.
raj (eng-sre): noted. leaving additional logs in INC-7821.
jamie (eng-oncall): thanks team. leaving handoff notes in #oncall-handoffs and marking this thread as resolved for immediate paging. will reopen if regressions reappear. :white_check_mark:
